title: How do we add by changing everything to hundredths?
description: Two lengths in units, tenths and hundredths are each changed to a count of hundredths, added, and changed back to units. Keeko changes the tenths to hundredths without multiplying.
teaching_notes: One idea: a unit is one hundred hundredths and a tenth is ten hundredths, so every part becomes a count of hundredths. Watch for students who write three tenths as three hundredths.

source: Add 15 3/10 4/100 and 2 6/10 8/100 again, this time by converting both to hundredths.
video_script.why: The child has added place by place and now adds the same two numbers by changing both to hundredths.
video_script.substitution: Change every part to hundredths, add the two counts, then change back to units and hundredths.
video_script.anchor: Two lengths, 15 3/10 4/100 and 2 6/10 8/100, each broken into units, tenths and hundredths
video_script.wrong_answer: one thousand five hundred seven hundredths
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko adds 3 tenths and 4 hundredths as 3 + 4 = 7 hundredths, but 3 tenths is 30 hundredths, so the count is 1534.
video_script.payoff_line: The sum is eighteen units and two hundredths
maths_rules: Slip: 3 tenths is 30 hundredths, not 3 hundredths.
video_script.design: One idea: change every part to hundredths, add the counts, change back. Assumes the child can add place by place. Wrong idea: count tenths as hundredths without ten times. The two numbers stay on the board.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; two lengths 15 3/10 4/100 and 2 6/10 8/100 with a plus sign between them

marks.book: the title card arrives: From your book
marks.two: the two lengths appear with a plus sign between them

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='two'/>We have the same two lengths to add as before.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Can we add them by changing both to hundredths?

beats.on_screen: the two lengths stay on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: one unit shown as 10 tenths, each tenth shown as 10 hundredths; labels 100 hundredths and 10 hundredths

marks.unit: a unit glows with the label 100 hundredths
marks.tenth: a tenth glows with the label 10 hundredths

narration: <bookmark mark='unit'/>One unit holds one hundred hundredths, and one tenth holds ten hundredths.
<bookmark mark='tenth'/>This lets us count every part of a length in hundredths.

marks.given: the two lengths are written one under the other

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, fifteen units, three tenths, and four hundredths, and two units, six tenths, and eight hundredths.

beats.on_screen: To find: the sum, using hundredths

marks.find: the words the sum are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the sum by using hundredths.

marks.one: 15 units, 3 tenths and 4 hundredths change to 1500, 30 and 4 hundredths

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, the first length. Fifteen units are one thousand five hundred hundredths, and three tenths are thirty hundredths.
<bookmark mark='total'/>With four hundredths more, it is one thousand five hundred thirty four hundredths.

marks.two: 2 units, 6 tenths and 8 hundredths change to 200, 60 and 8 hundredths

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step two, the second length. Two units are two hundred, and six tenths are sixty, and eight more.
<bookmark mark='total'/>Together that is two hundred sixty eight hundredths.

marks.add: 1534 and 268 are added over the same 100 to give 1802/100

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step three, add the counts. Both are in hundredths, so we add them as whole numbers. The total is one thousand eight hundred two hundredths.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Step four, change back to units, because one thousand eight hundred hundredths are eighteen whole units.
<bookmark mark='units'/>Only two hundredths are left over after that, and they stay as hundredths.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The sum is eighteen units and two hundredths.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 15 3/10 4/100 = 1500 + 3 + 4 = 1507 hundredths; a tenth bar with 10 hundredths in it sits beside 3 tenths; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.fix: the bubble is struck through and 3 tenths is shown as 30 hundredths

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko says the first length is one thousand five hundred seven hundredths, because three and four make seven.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But a tenth holds ten hundredths. Three tenths are thirty hundredths, so the count is much bigger.
